transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-04
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Cerulean Head of Partnerships), Lina Gomez (Cloud Partnerships), Marcus Liu (Solutions Architect)

Summary: Intro / partner discovery call to explore integration between Redwood Inference and Cerulean Cloud (private cloud + managed GPU offering). Discussed business motion, technical integration points (VPC peering, dedicated capacity, private control plane), and next steps for MOU and technical deep dive.

Topics: partnership model, integration options (marketplace vs managed offering vs joint go-to-market), technical constraints (VPC, KMS, data residency), benchmarks and pilot scope.

Action items (captured verbally during call): see metadata action_items.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — super excited. Quick intro from Redwood side: I'm Ava, AE, and this is Diego, our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Ravi Patel: Hey Ava, thanks. I'm Ravi, run partnerships at Cerulean. Lina and Marcus from infra are here.
[00:18] Lina Gomez: hi all.
[00:22] Diego Morales: quick nod, hey. So agenda — quick intros, what you're looking for in a partner, 10-15 minute tech constraints + open questions, then next steps. Sound good?
[00:30] Marcus Liu: yup. We have about 40 minutes.
[00:34] Ava Chen: great. Can you start with a quick overview of Cerulean's offering and what you hope a Redwood partnership would enable?
[00:43] Ravi Patel: sure, Cerulean is managed private cloud focused on regulated customers — we do regionally isolated clusters and we also have a managed GPU marketplace. Our customers want pre-baked ML infra that is certifiable. We're exploring partnerships to offer an inference runtime and managed model catalog — so ideally an integration where Redwood appears as a verified runtime in our marketplace and we can offer Dedicated capacity as a co-managed option.
[01:12] Ava Chen: got it. So you're looking for a commerce + technical integration — marketplace listing but also an option to provision dedicated pools for bigger customers?
[01:21] Ravi Patel: exactly. Some of our larger customers will want private deployments or VPC peering; others will use hosted APIs.
[01:28] Diego Morales: quick question for Marcus — what's the typical network topology customers spin up? Are you doing tenant VPCs with peering or full transit VPC?
[01:37] Marcus Liu: most are tenant VPCs with peering to our management plane. For high-security customers we offer air-gapped options. We also have KMS integrations (we support AWS KMS + HashiCorp Vault).
[01:49] Diego Morales: good — that maps to Redwood Private well. We support VPC peering, private control plane, and on-prem packages. One note: our Dedicated product is a reserved GPU pool you can offer as a SKU; we can also do a managed offering where Cerulean provisions the infra and we provide the runtime.
[02:08] Lina Gomez: what's the overhead for running the runtime — like does it require specific GPU drivers, and what about quantization — we need to know the compatibility with our GPU images.
[02:17] Diego Morales: we support common NVIDIA stacks, and for some newer kernels we do optimized builds. Quantization is supported, but we call it quantisization sometimes in docs — sorry, bad pronounciation — we have recommendations per model. We typically ship a container image that your infra team can run; for our Private installs we have an installer that integrates with local KMS or HSM.
[02:38] Marcus Liu: ok, container image plus an operator?
[02:42] Diego Morales: yeah, operator or helm charts. For the managed marketplace flow, the integration is simpler — we surface endpoints and billing via your marketplace. For a co-managed dedicated sku, we'll want to work through autoscaling policies and how burst capacity is exposed.
[03:00] Ravi Patel: licensing/commerce question — are there minimum commitments for Dedicated? Because some customers balk at multi-month commits.
[03:07] Ava Chen: Dedicated usually has reserved commit options with monthly or annual contracts. We also support burst/spot capacity on top for short-term needs. For marketplaces we can do pay-as-you-go hosted API access too.
[03:19] Lina Gomez: security stuff — SOC2, audit logs, SSO. We need answers for those for our compliance checklist. Do you have SOC2?
[03:26] Ava Chen: yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II, we have ISO on the roadmap and an enterprise compliance pack. We can share our security pack (SOC2 report, pen test summaries, SAML SSO docs).
[03:36] Marcus Liu: KMS question — if we do a private deployment, keys must be customer-managed.
[03:40] Diego Morales: supported — we integrate with customer KMS/HSMs and support key rotation policies.
[03:45] [sound of typing] Speaker 1: 
[03:48] Ravi Patel: timeline — we're planning to announce marketplace partners in Q4; pilot customers for managed GPU SKU in Q3. What's a realistic onboard timeline for Redwood?
[03:58] Ava Chen: for a marketplace listing and hosted API integration, we can be live in 4–6 weeks typical (docs, test account, basic listing). For Dedicated/co-managed SKUs and Private installs, 6–12 weeks depending on legal and integrations.
[04:12] Marcus Liu: for Private installs, how invasive is the installer? We try to avoid agents running on customer hosts.
[04:18] Diego Morales: installer is optional — we have operator-based deployment and a fully-managed option where we run runtime in a tenant-controlled cluster. There's some orchestration required for KV cache management and GPU kernel setup but we provide automation.
[04:30] Lina Gomez: something we see a lot: customers care about inference latency and cost. Can you explain how you balance batching/caching vs latency SLOs?
[04:39] Diego Morales: sure — Redwood's runtime does continuous batching and prefix/KV caching; you can set latency SLOs per route. For low-latency, we reduce batching and lean on fast kernels + reserved capacity; for throughput-focused workloads we enable batching and cache warmers. We also provide recommendations via Redwood Optimize to tune quantization and batching.
[04:59] Ravi Patel: curious about benchmark validation — customers ask for third-party benchmarks. Do you provide a benchmark harness?
[05:06] Diego Morales: we have a benchmark template and can run benchmarks in our infra or provide a harness for you to run; we'll provide a spreadsheet with token/sec, p99 latencies for common models. We'll also help design the test set — usually we recommend a mix of customer flows.
[05:19] Marcus Liu: for regulated customers we need audit logs and trace-level request IDs tied to SSO.
[05:24] Ava Chen: audit logs and request tracing are standard; we can ship logs to your logging endpoint or perform integrations with SIEMs.
[05:31] Ravi Patel: what about data residency — some customers require regional hosting.
[05:35] Ava Chen: Hosted API runs in multiple regions; Dedicated/Private can be deployed in the customer's region or on-prem. We'll need a regional footprint discussion for the big customers.
[05:44] [00:06 pause] Speaker 2: 
[05:46] Lina Gomez: any potential blockers you typically see?
[05:49] Diego Morales: blockers tend to be legal (contract comms), KMS/HSM policy alignment, and in some cases GPU driver or kernel mismatches on custom images. We mitigate with an early infra checklist and a short validation run.
[06:02] Ravi Patel: pricing question — do you support reseller/partner margins? For marketplace SKUs we'd want a partner margin or referral fee.
[06:11] Ava Chen: yes, we have partner pricing options and referral fee structures; we can share a draft partner MOU.
[06:18] Marcus Liu: technical — for model variants, do you do automatic fallback to smaller models when capacity is constrained?
[06:25] Diego Morales: we have smart routing policies — route by latency/cost/region, and fallback to compatible model variants if capacity runs low. There can be quality tradeoffs but we can configure fallback policies per customer.
[06:36] Lina Gomez: any known integrations with cloud marketplaces?
[06:39] Ava Chen: we've integrated with a few — will share examples.
[06:42] Ravi Patel: competitor concerns — some customers use Lambda Labs or Paperspace; how's Redwood differentiated?
[06:47] Ava Chen: Redwood is production-first with strong observability, rollout controls (canary/A-B), and cost-aware controls. We focus on inference economics — batch, cache, quantization — with tooling to measure regressions.
[07:00] Marcus Liu: okay, lets talk pilot scope. We have 2 pilot customers: 1) fintech customer with strict data residency in EU, needs VPC peering + customer KMS; 2) adtech customer heavy on throughput, cost sensitive.
[07:13] Diego Morales: for fintech: recommend Private deployment + customer-managed KMS, dedicated pools; for adtech: Dedicated with aggressive batching, maybe lower precision quantization. We'll propose model/quantization profiles.
[07:26] Ava Chen: next step from our side: we can send a partner integration spec + draft MOU and a benchmark template. From technical side, Diego will own the deep dive and benchmark setup.
[07:36] Ravi Patel: good. For legal/compliance we'll need SOC2 and SSO docs.
[07:41] Ava Chen: we'll send security pack and a SAML SSO integration guide.
[07:46] [08:00 short background noise] Speaker 3: 
[07:50] Marcus Liu: one more specific — for our marketplace, we need an image you can provide that runs on our curated GPU image stack. What's the turnaround?
[07:58] Diego Morales: we can produce a certified container image in ~1–2 weeks for standard stacks; if kernel-level tuning is needed it might take longer. We'll need the exact image details.
[08:09] Lina Gomez: can you do an out-of-band test to measure cold-start p99s for a 2k token seq?
[08:14] Diego Morales: yes, we'll include that in the benchmark template.
[08:17] Ravi Patel: sounds good. Any legal IP concerns about model hosting? Some of our customers want to host their own models on partners.
[08:27] Ava Chen: customers can bring-your-own-model to Dedicated/Private installs. For hosted models we have terms outlining model licensing; we'll include language in the MOU.
[08:38] Marcus Liu: there was a tiny mention earlier — KV cache management — does it require sticky sessions?
[08:44] Diego Morales: KV cache can be shard-aware; we provide both in-memory and external cache options. Sticky session helps warm cache but we can also do distributed cache with pinning.
[08:55] Lina Gomez: ok.
[08:57] [09:00] Speaker 1 (unlabeled):
[09:02] Ava Chen: wrapping up — to recap, Redwood will: 1) send integration spec & partner MOU by Aug 11; 2) share benchmark template and sample results; 3) provide SOC2/security pack and SSO docs; 4) Diego to schedule technical deep dive with Marcus and infra team week of Aug 17. Cerulean to provide customer list and infra diagrams by Aug 10.
[09:26] Ravi Patel: that aligns. We'll also send sample customer requirements & priority list.
[09:31] Ava Chen: perfect. Any show-stoppers we didn't cover?
[09:34] Marcus Liu: none immediate, just the usual legal/compliance and KMS alignment.
[09:39] Lina Gomez: agree.
[09:41] Ava Chen: ok we'll follow up in email with links — integration spec (https://redwood.ai/partners/cerulean-integration-spec), partner MOU draft (link), and benchmark spreadsheet.
[09:53] Ravi Patel: thanks all.
[09:55] Ava Chen: thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
